facts.fact: Ittan's writing case holds an unfinished letter to his wife's physicians (boil the willow bark, she likes the window open in rain) and, beneath it, an oilcloth bundle tied with red thread holding Chathu's contract chit (a hide strip naming the warden's chamber, death by beast, before the pass closes) and the payment writ.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the effects, the letter, the chit and the writ.

facts.fact: The payment writ is dated seven weeks before the wedding, payable to the Resin House on the warden's account, sealed in the queen's green wax with the sunbird; the seal matches the wedding-gift seal, including a small chip at the left wing tip.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the two seals to match.

facts.fact: Neela and Devan hide the oilcloth bundle under the third slat of the warden's chamber, telling neither Muthu nor the clerk.
facts.why: needed to secure the evidence after the reveal.

facts.fact: Nine days into the rains Muthu returns from the Resin House fodder run: he laid the cloth in Kirri's cage, she lay on it with the anklet still on, and he saw Chathu on the cook-house step holding a black-covered book to his chest.
facts.why: needed for the teaser, with Kirri in the kennels and Chathu holding the ledger.
